scope: Vehicle Tracking System (VTS) — fleet trips, vehicles, locations, routes, GPS telemetry, and exception alerts.

critical_join_rules.trip_to_vehicle: JOIN vehicle v ON trip.vehicle_id = v.id — always show v.vehicle_number NOT vehicle.id
critical_join_rules.trip_to_location: LEFT JOIN location l ON trip.location_id = l.id — show l.name
critical_join_rules.trip_to_route: LEFT JOIN route r ON trip.route_id = r.id — show r.route_code
critical_join_rules.trip_to_status: LEFT JOIN trip_log tl ON trip.recent_state_id = tl.id LEFT JOIN trip_status_master tsm ON tl.trip_status_master_id = tsm.id — show tsm.display_type as status
critical_join_rules.route_to_source_location: LEFT JOIN location sl ON route.source_location_id = sl.id — show sl.name AS source_location
critical_join_rules.route_to_dest_location: LEFT JOIN location dl ON route.destination_location_id = dl.id — show dl.name AS destination_location
critical_join_rules.exception_to_vehicle: JOIN vehicle v ON vts_exception.vehicle_id = v.id — show v.vehicle_number
critical_join_rules.transaction_to_vehicle: JOIN vehicle v ON vts_transaction.vehicle_id = v.id

important_column_notes.trip.recent_state_id: FK to trip_log.id (most recent log entry). To get status: JOIN trip_log tl ON trip.recent_state_id = tl.id JOIN trip_status_master tsm ON tl.trip_status_master_id = tsm.id. Use tsm.display_type.
important_column_notes.trip.is_active: bit(1). For active trips: WHERE trip.is_active = 1
important_column_notes.vehicle.vehicle_number: Human-readable vehicle plate number. Always use in SELECT and WHERE, not vehicle.id
important_column_notes.location.name: Human-readable location name. Always SELECT this not location.id
important_column_notes.route.route_code: Human-readable route code. Use in SELECT and WHERE
important_column_notes.trip_status_master.display_type: User-friendly status label (En route, Created, Cancel). Always SELECT this

business_relationships.trip_status_flow: trip.recent_state_id -> trip_log.id -> trip_status_master.id gives current status
business_relationships.route_locations: route.source_location_id and route.destination_location_id both reference location.id
business_relationships.vehicle_exceptions: vts_exception.vehicle_id = vehicle.id — overspeed, halt, route_deviation counts per vehicle
business_relationships.trip_log_history: trip_log is append-only — one row per status change. Full lifecycle history of any trip.

example_correct_queries.question: Show active trips with vehicle numbers
example_correct_queries.sql: SELECT t.name AS trip_name, v.vehicle_number, l.name AS location, tsm.display_type AS status FROM trip t LEFT JOIN vehicle v ON t.vehicle_id = v.id LEFT JOIN location l ON t.location_id = l.id LEFT JOIN trip_log tl ON t.recent_state_id = tl.id LEFT JOIN trip_status_master tsm ON tl.trip_status_master_id = tsm.id WHERE t.company_id = {company_id} AND t.is_active = 1 ORDER BY t.date_created DESC LIMIT 50

example_correct_queries.question: Show all routes with source and destination
example_correct_queries.sql: SELECT r.route_code, sl.name AS source_location, dl.name AS destination_location FROM route r LEFT JOIN location sl ON r.source_location_id = sl.id LEFT JOIN location dl ON r.destination_location_id = dl.id WHERE r.company_id = {company_id} AND r.is_active = 1

example_correct_queries.question: Which vehicle overspeeded the most
example_correct_queries.sql: SELECT v.vehicle_number, SUM(COALESCE(ve.over_speed_count, 0)) AS total_overspeed_events FROM vts_exception ve JOIN vehicle v ON ve.vehicle_id = v.id WHERE ve.company_id = {company_id} AND COALESCE(ve.over_speed_count, 0) > 0 GROUP BY v.vehicle_number ORDER BY total_overspeed_events DESC LIMIT 1

never_do: Never join on display fields: do NOT write trip.vehicle_id = vehicle.vehicle_number — always join on IDs
Never expose internal IDs in SELECT output — resolve to display names
Never write INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on trip_log or vts_transaction — they are read-only
Never omit company_id WHERE clause for trip, vehicle, route, vts_exception
